next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar

glance_notes.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Mail Ballot State: Colorado conducts its regular elections primarily by mail. County clerks automatically mail ballots to active registered electors at their registered mailing addresses, while in-person voting remains available at Voter Service and Polling Centers.

glance_notes.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Election Day Registration: Eligible Colorado residents can register and vote in person at a Voter Service and Polling Center through 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 Mail-Ballot Registration Deadline: October 26, 2026 is the deadline to submit a registration application by mail, through a voter registration agency or driver's license office, or online and still receive a ballot by mail for the November 3 General Election. Registration remains available after that date, but voters registering during the final seven days must obtain a ballot in person at a Voter Service and Polling Center.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Colorado residents can register online through GoVoteColorado if they have a valid Social Security number, Colorado driver's license, or Colorado identification card. A paper registration form is available for people who cannot use the online system. To vote, you must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old by Election Day, and have resided in Colorado for at least 22 days immediately before the election. Colorado also permits preregistration beginning at age 15, but a preregistered person cannot vote until eligible.
register.glance_value: Register online, by paper, or in person
register.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
register.internal_note: Go Vote Colorado directly provides online registration and the official paper form. Supplemental verification source: Colorado Secretary of State voter registration form — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/NVRA/files/COVoterRegistrationAgency.pdf](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/NVRA/files/COVoterRegistrationAgency.pdf) — establishes citizenship, 22-day residency and voting-age requirements. Colorado's preregistration age was reduced to 15 effective January 1, 2025 by SB24-210. Registration identification is separate from identification required when voting.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use GoVoteColorado to find your voter registration record, review or update your registration information, check your mail-ballot status, view your sample ballot when available, and access ballot-tracking and ballot-curing services.
check_registration.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
check_registration.internal_note: The official Go Vote Colorado portal directly provides Find My Registration, mail-ballot status, sample-ballot access, BallotTrax and Txt2Cure services.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Colorado allows voter registration through Election Day, but the method and timing affect how you receive your ballot. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 26 is the deadline to register by mail, through a voter registration agency or driver's license examination facility, or online and still receive a ballot by mail. Beginning October 27, a newly registering voter will not be mailed a ballot and must visit a Voter Service and Polling Center to obtain one. Eligible voters can register and vote in person through 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.
deadlines.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar directly establishes October 26 as the final registration date for receiving a ballot by mail, the October 27 transition to in-person ballot issuance, and Election Day registration availability under Title 1, C.R.S.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Colorado uses Voter Service and Polling Centers rather than requiring voters to use a single assigned neighborhood polling place. Use GoVoteColorado to find voting centers and ballot drop boxes available for your election. Locations and operating hours are established by county election officials and can vary.
polling_place.glance_value: Use any eligible VSPC in your county
polling_place.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
polling_place.internal_note: Go Vote Colorado is the official state portal for locating voting centers and drop boxes and contacting county clerks. Colorado's mail-ballot/VSPC system is governed by Title 1, Article 5, C.R.S. County election plans determine individual VSPC locations and operating schedules.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Colorado voters can vote in person at a Voter Service and Polling Center on Election Day even though active registered voters are generally mailed ballots. At a voting center, voters can register or update their registration, obtain and vote a ballot, or receive assistance with voting. A voter who is in line by 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote.
election_day.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
election_day.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Colorado Secretary of State 2026 Election Calendar — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf) — establishes Election Day and 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. polling hours. Current Colorado election law preserves voting for eligible electors present at the polling location by closing time.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Colorado Voter Service and Polling Centers are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. An eligible voter who is at the voting location at or before 7:00 p.m. must be allowed to vote. Someone arriving after 7:00 p.m. is not entitled to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Calendar directly states that polls are open 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. for the November 3 General Election. Current statutory authority is Title 1, C.R.S.; the requirement to permit eligible electors present by 7:00 p.m. to vote is established by Colorado election law.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Colorado provides in-person voting before Election Day through Voter Service and Polling Centers. Opening dates, locations and daily hours vary by county and location, with additional centers required as Election Day approaches. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, use GoVoteColorado or your county clerk's election information to find currently open voting centers and their hours.
early_voting.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
early_voting.internal_note: Colorado's VSPC system provides voting before Election Day, but locations and operating hours are county-specific and should not be generalized into one statewide daily schedule. HB26-1113, signed June 1, 2026, modified several VSPC requirements, including campus-center timing. Current 2026 law was considered when drafting this section.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Colorado automatically sends a mail ballot to active registered voters for statewide elections, so voters do not need an excuse or a traditional absentee-ballot application. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 26 is the last day to register or update your registration through the ordinary remote methods and still receive a ballot by mail. Completed ballots must be received by the county clerk no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day; a postmark does not make a late-arriving ordinary mail ballot timely. You can return your ballot through the mail, an official drop box, or an authorized voting location. BallotTrax is available to track your ballot.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Mail ballot automatically sent to active voters
absentee_mail.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
absentee_mail.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Colorado Secretary of State 2026 Election Calendar — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf) — establishes October 26 as the last registration date to receive a ballot by mail and states that ordinary ballots must be in the county clerk's hands by 7:00 p.m. Election Day. Go Vote Colorado provides BallotTrax and voting/drop-box location services. Military and overseas ballots have a different receipt rule addressed separately.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Colorado voters voting in person must provide an acceptable form of identification. Accepted identification includes several photo and non-photo documents authorized by Colorado law, such as a valid Colorado driver's license or identification card, U.S. passport, qualifying government employee ID, pilot's license, military ID, Medicare or Medicaid card, certified birth certificate, qualifying student ID, tribal identification, or certain current government or financial documents showing the voter's name and Colorado address. Some forms may be presented digitally where permitted by law. A Social Security number or its last four digits is not identification for voting in person. Special documentation rules apply to residents of qualifying group residential facilities.
voter_id.glance_value: Acceptable ID required for in-person voting
voter_id.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
voter_id.internal_note: Go Vote Colorado provides the official Acceptable Forms of ID resource. Supplemental authoritative source: Colorado Secretary of State Election Rules, Rule 30 — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?ruleVersionId=5364](https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?ruleVersionId=5364) — establishes identification requirements for in-person and mail voting and confirms that a Social Security number is not voting ID. HB26-1113, effective in 2026, expanded the statutory definition of identification to include additional documents including a Division of Youth Services identification card and specified correspondence for electors confined in county jails or detention facilities. Because registration identifiers and voting ID serve different purposes, they are not conflated here.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Colorado provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities. Voter Service and Polling Centers provide accessible voting systems for in-person voting, and voters may receive assistance as permitted by election law. Colorado also provides accessible electronic ballot-delivery options for eligible voters who cannot independently read, mark, or print a ballot because of a disability. The official GoVoteColorado portal provides the state's current accessible-voting resources and county contact information.
accessible_voting.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
accessible_voting.internal_note: Go Vote Colorado links directly to the Secretary of State's Accessible Voting resource. Supplemental authoritative source: current Colorado Election Rules, 8 CCR 1505-1, Rule 11.6, requires voting systems used by people with disabilities to be certified by the Secretary of State. SB24-210 updated accessible voting-system standards to align with federal standards.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Colorado provides special registration and ballot procedures for military members, their eligible family members, and U.S. citizens living overseas under UOCAVA. Covered voters can request electronic ballot delivery and may use federal military-and-overseas voting forms. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, counties must transmit ballots to military and overseas voters by the applicable 45-day federal deadline. A qualifying military or overseas ballot must be sent no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day and received by the county clerk by the close of business on November 12, 2026 to be counted.
military_overseas.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
military_overseas.internal_note: Go Vote Colorado links to the official Military & Overseas Voters resource. Supplemental authoritative source: Colorado Election Rules, Rule 16 — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?ruleVersionId=7573](https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?ruleVersionId=7573) — governs UOCAVA voting and electronic ballot transmission. Colorado Secretary of State 2026 Election Calendar — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf) — establishes that UOCAVA ballots must be sent by 7:00 p.m. Election Day and received by close of business on the eighth day after the election, November 12, 2026.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student can register in Colorado if the student establishes Colorado as their sole legal voting residence and otherwise meets the state's eligibility requirements. Attending school in Colorado by itself does not automatically establish voting residence. Colorado's residence rules consider whether the student intends the Colorado location to be their home. A student whose primary voting residence remains in another state should not register in Colorado solely because they attend school there.
student_voting.glance_value: Residence depends on where you make your home
student_voting.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Election Rules
student_voting.internal_note: Colorado Election Rules directly address student residence. The rules state that a student attending college in Colorado is likely a resident when the student presently intends to make the district their home, while an out-of-state student with no intent to make the district a permanent home is likely not a resident. HB26-1113 also modified voter-information requirements for institutions of higher education in 2026.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Use GoVoteColorado to view your official sample ballot when it becomes available. The ballot shown is tied to your voter record so that you can review the contests and questions applicable to you before voting. County clerks have the most complete information about county and local contests.
sample_ballot.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official Go Vote Colorado portal directly provides a View My Sample Ballot function. Local ballot content is administered by the applicable county election official.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Colorado Secretary of State, Elections Division, 1700 Broadway, Suite 550, Denver, CO 80290. Phone: 303-894-2200. Fax: 303-869-4861. Email: elections@coloradosos.gov. For voter-registration records, mail ballots, voting-center locations and other county-administered election services, contact your county clerk and recorder.
contact.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
contact.internal_note: Contact details independently verified from the Colorado Secretary of State Elections Division's current official Elections Data Request form — [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/forms/dataRequests.pdf](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/forms/dataRequests.pdf) — which lists 1700 Broadway, Suite 550, Denver, CO 80290; 303-894-2200; 303-869-4861; and [elections@coloradosos.gov](mailto:elections@coloradosos.gov). Go Vote Colorado provides the official Contact My County Clerk service.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use GoVoteColorado for voter registration, registration updates, registration lookup, sample ballots, mail-ballot status, BallotTrax, ballot curing, voting-center and drop-box information, accessible-voting resources, military and overseas voting information, and county-clerk contacts. Colorado elections are administered locally by county clerks and recorders under state election law and rules, so your county clerk is the primary local authority for ballot delivery and local voting locations.
official_resources.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State — Go Vote Colorado
official_resources.internal_note: Official election-law and rule repository: [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/lawsRulesResources.html](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/lawsRulesResources.html). Official 2026 Election Calendar: [https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/calendars/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf). Current 2026 Colorado Revised Statutes are available through the Colorado General Assembly at [https://content.leg.colorado.gov/agencies/office-legislative-legal-services/2026-crs-titles-download](https://content.leg.colorado.gov/agencies/office-legislative-legal-services/2026-crs-titles-download). Go Vote Colorado provides direct links to county clerks and all major voter-facing state services.
